content: Alice Smith and I decided to use PostgreSQL over MySQL for the new Grove backend. Alice felt strongly that pgvector support was the deciding factor. We'll migrate the prototype SQLite data next sprint.
Had coffee with Bob Chen today at Elysian. He's moving to a new role at Shopify as Staff Engineer. We talked about distributed tracing and he recommended Honeycomb over Datadog for smaller teams.
Team retrospective is scheduled for Friday June 6 at 2pm in the main boardroom. Sarah, Diego, and I are attending. We'll cover the Q2 sprint results.
We chose React over Vue for the dashboard rebuild. The main reason was the larger ecosystem and the team's existing familiarity. Mark was the decision maker.
Caught up with Priya Nair at PyCon. She's leading the ML infra team at Stripe now. She mentioned they've open-sourced their feature store — worth checking out.
Doctor's appointment Tuesday March 18 at 9am at City Medical Centre. Remember to bring the referral from Dr. Patel.
After the incident last week we decided to migrate from Heroku to Fly.io. The main driver was cost: Heroku's new pricing was $250/mo versus $40 on Fly. Decision made by the whole eng team.
Lunch with James Forrest from Acme Corp. He's interested in a pilot of our analytics product. Next step: send him the pricing deck by EOW.
Board meeting on July 10 at 3pm, Zoom link in calendar. Agenda: Q2 results, Series B update, hiring plan.
Chose TypeScript over plain JavaScript for the new SDK. Strong typing will help third-party integrators. Decision driven by customer feedback from three enterprise accounts.

Met with Dr. Lisa Park at the AI in Healthcare conference. She runs the clinical NLP lab at Stanford. She's working on de-identification pipelines for medical notes — very relevant to what we're doing.
Dinner with the family Wednesday evening at 7pm. Booking at Trattoria Romana, 4 people.
After a long evaluation period the team decided on Terraform over Pulumi for infrastructure as code. The rationale: more online resources and existing team knowledge. I made the final call.
Had a 1:1 with Carlos Rivera, my engineering manager. He gave feedback that my technical writing has improved significantly. We set a goal to present at the next all-hands.
Onsite interview at Anthropic on Monday September 2 starting at 10am. Three rounds: system design, coding, culture. Contact is Emma Lawson from recruiting.
We went with Stripe for payments instead of Braintree. The developer experience is substantially better and the documentation is excellent. Unanimous team decision.
Networked with Yuki Tanaka from OpenAI DevRel at the Hackathon. She offered to help us get beta access to the new embeddings endpoint. I should follow up by email.
Quarterly planning kickoff Thursday at 9am in the Seattle office. Bring printed OKRs.
Decided to sunset the legacy SOAP API by end of Q3. Migration guide will be published two months prior. Decision owner is the platform team lead.
Ran into Ananya Rao at the grocery store — she's our former CTO. She mentioned she's advising three startups now and is happy to do a call about fundraising strategy.
Sprint planning Monday at 10am on Zoom. I need to prepare ticket estimates for the auth refactor epics.
We're adopting trunk-based development over feature branches. The experiment over the last month showed faster release cycles and fewer merge conflicts. Team consensus.
Coffee chat with Martin Fowler's talk on refactoring patterns really stuck with me — I should apply the strangler fig pattern to the monolith migration.
Dentist on October 3 at 11am. Bring insurance card.
Met Sarah Johnson from Notion at a meetup. She's working on their API v2. We exchanged contact details and agreed to compare notes on rate limiting strategies.
Finalized that we'll use Kafka over RabbitMQ for the event bus. Partition tolerance and replay capability were the deciding factors for our use case. I drove the decision after the POC.
Annual performance review with my manager Rachel next Tuesday at 2pm.
Video call with Wei Liu from Baidu Research about potential collaboration on our multilingual NLP work. He's interested in sharing datasets under a research agreement.
Team decided against adopting GraphQL for the public API — REST is simpler to document and our clients haven't asked for subscription-style updates. Decision by product + eng.
Workshop on async Python at PyBay conference August 14-15. I'm speaking on Saturday at 3pm about structured concurrency with anyio.
Just a random note about wanting to learn guitar. No specific decision or person involved, just a personal interest note.
Settled on using Pydantic v2 over dataclasses for our API models. The validation ergonomics and JSON schema generation made it the clear winner. I proposed it, team agreed.
